races.name: Bath Country Race Day, What A Way To Make Weekend! EBF Restricted Maiden Stakes (For Horses In Band D) (EBF Restricted Race Qualifier) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Anna Belardo
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner, which gives her a priceless tactical advantage in a six-runner field; trainer Dr Newland & Insole pairing has been cold (0/13 last 14 days) and she returns after 104 days off, but her control of the pace here is the dominant factor regardless of those concerns.

runners_data.name: Etienne
runners_data.note: Richard Spencer in good recent nick (2/16 T14) and Saffie Osborne takes the ride; posted a close second over 6f Good last time and steps back to 5½f with a clear class edge at OR-86 over most rivals — the form angle and ability make this horse the primary beneficiary if Anna Belardo's lead is catchable.

runners_data.name: Our Fella
runners_data.note: Raced just two days ago which is an obvious freshness concern on this surface, but the five-run profile shows consistent placing form at 5f on Good going (3 of 7 placed); apprentice Isobelle Chalmers claims 7lb and a hold-up style in a small field limits scope for a winning challenge unless the pace is fast.

runners_data.name: Tree Wizard
runners_data.note: Honest recent form showing multiple places but a naturally prominent style that this field's makeup has pushed into a midfield mapping — racing out of its preferred position reduces its effectiveness; the OR-66 also makes the class task steep against Etienne.

runners_data.name: Cotai Jaunt
runners_data.note: Sean Bowen takes a high-profile booking for Ollie Sangster (strong T14 at 3/30) and the OR-120 on debut is eye-catching, but the sole run was sixth over 6f on Standard, giving no guide to Good turf form or whether a hold-up style translates at 5½f.

runners_data.name: Polly The Sniper
runners_data.note: Two runs to date — fifth and sixth on Standard and Good — show limited encouragement, but a prominent style means she is at least racing in a position that suits the expected race shape; Tom Dascombe yard is quiet (0/9 T14) and the step to Bath 5½f needs proving.

races.paceDynamic: Anna Belardo is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine pace rival to pressure her, she is likely to set a measured, controlled tempo from stall to the line on this Good ground at Bath. Etienne and Polly The Sniper are the natural prominent types who will look to track close behind, while Tree Wizard — a genuine prominent racer — has been pushed into a midfield mapping because the field holds more pace-seeking types than can all secure their preferred berth, meaning Tree Wizard will likely be squeezed into a less comfortable position. Our Fella and Cotai Jaunt sit furthest back, but both operate from hold-up positions in a six-runner field where the real estate ahead will be tightly contested. With Anna Belardo dictating a sustainable, uncontested gallop, this race shape strongly favours horses who can travel prominently in behind and produce a clean, well-timed challenge in the final two furlongs — true hold-up patterns are unlikely to generate enough momentum late unless the tempo is falsely fast.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Anna Belardo Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Anna Belardo leads without challenge and sets a fair, controlled pace throughout the 5½f.
scenarios.body: Anna Belardo dictates every yard at a comfortable tempo on Good going, denying closers the necessary overpace to reel her in; horses racing prominently in behind — Etienne and Polly The Sniper — are best placed to mount the closest pursuit.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Strike Late
scenarios.trigger: If Etienne or Polly The Sniper track Anna Belardo closely and simply overpower her entering the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Anna Belardo's lead is pegged back by a prominent tracker with higher raw ability — Etienne's OR-86 gives a class edge that may tell late — and the winner emerges from that front pack rather than behind it.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Finisher Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves stronger than expected and late closers find a gap to pounce through the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Our Fella, with consistent placed form at this trip on Good going and five runs of experience, is the most likely beneficiary if there is any pace collapse; Cotai Jaunt is a runner on debut debutant who faces a steep ask without that form foundation.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Muddled Pace Scenario
scenarios.trigger: If the start is unruly or Anna Belardo fails to stride on cleanly, causing a compressed, tactical crawl.
scenarios.body: A genuinely slow pace over 5½f would compress the field and make the finish a sprint, potentially flattening the class advantage and opening the door for any runner who finds a clear run; Tree Wizard, forced out of its natural prominent role, could capitalise if it recovers that position.

watchPoints.text: Anna Belardo is unopposed on the front end — if she is allowed to bowl along at her own tempo unchallenged, her lead could prove very difficult to reel in over this distance; watch whether Etienne's rider attempts to close the gap early or gives her too much rope.

Our Fella ran only two days ago; monitor for any signs of fatigue or a jaded performance, as that turnaround could blunt what has otherwise been a consistent placed record at this course and distance profile.

Tree Wizard's true running style is prominent, but the field configuration means it may be unable to secure that berth — watch whether it gets shuffled back at the start or forced to settle wider and later than ideal, which would significantly compromise its chance.
Cotai Jaunt debuts on turf for a powerful yard with a big-name jockey; it is unexposed and the market move, if any, at the off is worth monitoring given the lack of form to anchor an assessment.

races.name: Welsh Power 20th Anniversary Handicap Stakes (Bath Summer Sprint Series Qualifier) (Div I)

runners_data.name: The Feminine Urge
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type redistibuted to lead by necessity — her six-run form string (073265) shows no front-running wins, and racing out of role is a significant concern; Ashley Lewis (3lb claimer) will need to find a rhythm quickly, and the 20-day break on Good ground she handles (12/15 sim-going) at least removes a fitness worry.
runners_data.comment: Rated 9 lb above her official mark, The Feminine Urge arrives here on the back of a second three starts back and a promising fifth last time out, with experience over today's trip and going working in her favour; the risk is that she remains winless in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Ten Club
runners_data.note: A 48-day absence is the primary flag here — last five runs span 7f on Firm and Standard, making this 5½f Good surface look a new challenge; the headgear (h) suggests keenness issues, and 1W2P from only five similar-going runs is modest; Finley Marsh inherits a tricky task from the back of the field.
runners_data.comment: Ten Club fell last time out, and has run over today's trip and going — his rating of 64 heads the field and he looks the chief interest here, even if he remains winless in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Ken Brulee
runners_data.note: Three-year-old with a recent win over 6f Good (1/6f/GOO in last five runs) and sharp form across the last six starts (174361) — headgear (p) adds a tactical edge, and Rob Hornby is a strong booking; two wins and three places from 12 similar-going runs underlines he handles these conditions, and he is among the most likely to secure a forward pitch naturally.
runners_data.comment: Ken Brulee arrives on the back of a win last time out and has run over today's trip and going, giving him solid claims here off 132 lb from stall 8; the main risk is that his last six starts also include a sixth two runs back, hinting at inconsistency.

runners_data.name: Starsong
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old hold-up specialist who is bumped into a midfield map position because the rear is congested; Alistair Rawlinson partners a horse with consistent placed form (355520) but a STYLE_FIT of 0.94 means he is unlikely to see his ideal closing shape materialise; headgear (p) and nine from 15 similar-going efforts suggest he handles the surface.
runners_data.comment: Starsong ran a cracker two starts back when finishing second, and her experience over today's trip and going are clear assets for a mare rated 62 by us — the main concern is a winless recent run of form that she must finally convert.

runners_data.name: It's A Mugs Game
runners_data.note: Ran just two days ago — freshness is the dominant concern before any analysis of style or form; mapped into midfield from a natural hold-up role, and a form string of 0-468 on faster ground without a win or place from four similar-going runs offers little encouragement for this competitive Bath sprint.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, It's A Mugs Game also returns just two days after his last outing, leaving little to work with; he has run over today's trip before, and stall one is a fact worth noting.

runners_data.name: Port Hedland
runners_data.note: One win from 15 similar-going runs tells its own story, yet that win came over 6f Good (1/6f/GOO) and Tony Carroll's 4/43 14-day record shows the stable is in modest form; mapped forward from a true hold-up base (STYLE_FIT 0.92), and a 10-day turnaround is not a problem; Kieren Fox will need luck if the pace softens.
runners_data.comment: Port Hedland showed he can win, landing a victory five starts back, but back-to-back eighths in recent starts are a concern; he has run over today's trip and going, returns after ten days, and carries 128 lb from stall six.

runners_data.name: Anglesey Lad
runners_data.note: 112-day absence is a serious flag for a horse who has not won on Good ground in his last five outings (0W4P from 15 similar-going runs); Scott Dixon's 0/19 14-day record adds trainer concern; mapped into midfield from a natural rear-running style, and the lack of recent sharpness over 5½f makes this tough.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and returning after 112 days off, Anglesey Lad has experience of today's trip and conditions, yet his recent string of fourths and fifths — including a second four starts back — suggests he finds winning difficult, and a mark of 45 keeps him competitive.

runners_data.name: Rinky Tinky Tinky
runners_data.note: Four-year-old mare who handles Good ground (1W1P from 15 runs) but recent form reads poorly (-56580); Alice Bond's 5lb claim is attractive in a handicap, and headgear (p) has been fitted to sharpen her up; held-up naturally but redistributed forward — her STYLE_FIT of 0.90 suggests she is unlikely to reproduce a prominent-horse win from this position.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked seventh of nine on our figures, Rinky Tinky Tinky faces a stiff task, though she has run over today's distance and going before and returns on a sharp 11-day turnaround carrying 126 lb from stall two.

runners_data.name: My Boy Jack
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old veteran with headgear (v) fitted — has placed on Good ground (0W1P from five similar-going runs) but recent form (503440) is uninspiring; Olivia Haines (7lb claimer) gives a weight advantage, though the horse's natural rear-running style is squeezed into midfield by the crowded hold-up contingent, and 10 days since last run is not a concern.

races.paceDynamic: The Feminine Urge is the sole confirmed front-runner in this field and will be redistributed to lead by default, setting a measured, uncontested gallop on Good ground over 5½f at Bath — a course where the long run-in from the final bend rewards those who can sustain their effort rather than produce a late burst. With no genuine pace rival to pressurise her, she is likely to dictate at a controlled tempo, which classically compresses the winning margin and keeps the door open for those tracking closely. The race shape consequently favours horses that can race prominently or in the first half of the field and pick up efficiently off a steady pace, rather than pure closers needing a searching gallop to get involved. This field carries far more hold-up types than can realistically secure their natural position: Ken Brulee, Starsong, It's A Mugs Game, Port Hedland, Anglesey Lad, Rinky Tinky Tinky, and My Boy Jack are all redistributed or mapped forward of their natural role; of those, Ken Brulee (headgear: p, sharp recent form) and Starsong (headgear: p, consistent at this trip) are the most likely to organically press forward and take up a prominent berth closest to The Feminine Urge.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If The Feminine Urge sets an uncontested pace and none of the hold-up types can close the gap from off the pace on a steady tempo.
scenarios.body: The Feminine Urge controls every yard, and the winner emerges from the horses that have tracked closest throughout, with the long Bath run-in suiting those who have conserved energy by racing prominently.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If one of the horses mapped forward of their natural role settles close to the pace and picks up smoothly when the leader begins to tie up inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A horse like Ken Brulee or Starsong, racing in a forward position, exploits the moderate early gallop by sitting within a length or two and accelerating past the leader near the line.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Closes Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is faster than expected or The Feminine Urge sets a stronger gallop that strings the field out and leaves a gap for a genuine closer.
scenarios.body: One of the true hold-up types — Port Hedland or Anglesey Lad — finds the extra ground they need and charges through beaten horses late, though the steady Bath track and likely moderate tempo make this an uphill task.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Collapse and Reshuffle
scenarios.trigger: If The Feminine Urge fails to handle her redistributed front-running role and fades badly, causing a scramble among horses that were never in their natural position.
scenarios.body: With no natural leader in the field, a ragged early pace produces a messy race in which the most adaptable or best-weighted horse benefits from the chaos rather than the best-placed stylist.

watchPoints.text: The Feminine Urge is racing completely out of her natural hold-up role as the sole pace-setter — if she fails to stride out willingly or Ashley Lewis cannot settle her, the tempo will be false from the start and the whole race shape breaks down.

Ken Brulee has headgear (p) fitted and Rob Hornby aboard — if he jumps smartly and tracks The Feminine Urge closely, he becomes the chief danger at a course where the long run-in rewards prominent racers; watch for him moving into contention from the 2f marker.

It's A Mugs Game ran only two days ago — monitor market moves and any late withdrawal; if she contests this race at all, fatigue could cause her to drop back sharply in the straight and interfere with closers behind her.

With seven of nine runners redistibuted from their natural hold-up positions, the midfield group may bunch tightly in the early stages — Kieren Fox (Port Hedland) and Kieran O'Neill (Anglesey Lad) will need clean passage around the bend, and any interference could affect multiple runners simultaneously.

Starsong's consistency (355520) makes him a shape-dependent place threat — if the pace does quicken late and create a gap, Alistair Rawlinson has the experience to find the rail on the run-in; watch where he is positioned at halfway as a guide to his winning chance.

races.name: Welsh Power 20th Anniversary Handicap Stakes (Bath Summer Sprint Series Qualifier) (Div II)

runners_data.name: Up The Anti
runners_data.note: Long-absent handicapper (106 days off) for Tony Carroll, best form has come over 6f rather than 5½f, with only 3 runs from 15 on similar going producing zero wins or places — the trip and fitness query are real concerns on return.
runners_data.comment: Ranked top of the field on our figures, Up The Anti has run over today's trip and going and shapes as a leading threat from stall seven carrying 135 lb, though her recent pulled-up effort and winless run in her last six starts gives clear cause for caution after 106 days off.

runners_data.name: Honour Your Dreams
runners_data.note: On a going basis, she has 7 runs from 15 in similar conditions with one place, and although a natural prominent racer pushed to the front by default, she will set the pace here and her chance rises if the tempo stays comfortable; tongue tie adds a focus angle for Michael Attwater.
runners_data.comment: Fifth last time out and fourth two starts back, Honour Your Dreams arrives here on a reasonable footing after 36 days away, with experience over today's trip and going working in his favour, though he remains yet to win in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Geemann
runners_data.note: Ran just two days ago which is a significant freshness concern, but his form reads well with back-to-back thirds at 6f on Good ground and trainer Joe Tickle runs him quickly suggesting confidence; he is the most consistently placed horse in the race over similar conditions.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Geemann at least shows consistency with back-to-back thirds in recent outings, and he has experience of today's distance and going; however, a run just two days ago and a lowly official mark of 53 are both factors that temper expectations from stall two.

runners_data.name: Ten Cuidado
runners_data.note: Primarily a 7-8f horse stepping back sharply in trip, with only 1 run from 6 in similar going producing no win or place — Rob Hornby takes the ride but the shorter distance and his true hold-up style finding itself pushed to midfield both work against him here.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with two unplaced efforts among them, Ten Cuidado is hard to fancy ranked seventh of nine on our figures; he does at least return on a quick turnaround with experience of today's trip and conditions, and carries a workable 130 lb from stall four.

runners_data.name: Cici's Secret
runners_data.note: Edward Greatrex rides a mare flagged as fading in finishes, with five runs on similar Going producing zero wins or places and a consistent pattern of weakening late — that fade flag combined with an OR of 50 makes her a tough sell at the business end of a sprint.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Cici's Secret nonetheless rates above her official mark and has experience over today's trip, making her a stronger threat than her bare form suggests; the risk is that recent finishes have been modest and another flat effort could see her swallowed up.

runners_data.name: Sisters In The Sky
runners_data.note: Tyler Heard partners a seven-year-old veteran with solid placed form (two 3rds, a 4th and a 2nd in last five), her true hold-up tendencies nudging her into a midfield berth she cannot escape easily; on Good going she has placed 4 times from 15, suggesting she finds the surface fair.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts but often finding the frame, Sisters In The Sky arrives on a sharp 16-day turnaround with distance and going experience in his favour; the 126 lb burden and a mid-pack ranking give connections plenty to overcome.

runners_data.name: I Was Thinking
runners_data.note: Adrian Wintle's five-year-old returns after 33 days and has just 1 run from 8 on similar going producing a single place — his natural hold-up style is squeezed into a midfield pack, and his 6f form is more consistent than his recent 8f efforts suggest.
runners_data.comment: Yet to score in his last five starts, I Was Thinking nonetheless showed ability with a third two runs back and arrives here 33 days fresh, with experience of today's trip and going; the concern is that latest ninth suggests he needs to bounce back sharply.

runners_data.name: Daley T
runners_data.note: William Carson partners a lightly-handicapped six-year-old for Tony Carroll (who also saddles Up The Anti), with 5 runs from 15 on Good returning one place; his true prominent leanings are absorbed into midfield here, and a last-ten run of 80 at 6f makes the form hard to trust.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Daley T faces a stiff task here; a fourth three starts back and a third five starts back are the only recent bright spots for a gelding who arrives on a quick ten-day turnaround carrying 126 lb from stall 3.

runners_data.name: Rogue Rebellion
runners_data.note: Luke Morris rides the most consistently placed horse across differing ground types — 5th, 4th, 3rd, 4th, 3rd in last five — and his Good-going record of 8 runs from 15 with 2 places is the best strike rate among the hold-up types; his natural finishing style suits a scenario where the pace is stronger than expected.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Rogue Rebellion has an official rating of just 46 and ranks eighth of nine on our figures, making him hard to fancy despite the experience over today's trip and going and a return after a 24-day break.

races.paceDynamic: Honour Your Dreams is the sole confirmed pace-setter in this nine-runner sprint, redistributed from a natural prominent role to the front because no other horse is likely to take up the running — at Good going over 5½f at Bath, she sets what should be a steady, uncontested tempo with no rival likely to pressure her through the early stages. The bulk of the field — Ten Cuidado, Cici's Secret, Sisters In The Sky, I Was Thinking, Daley T, and Rogue Rebellion — are all genuine hold-up or prominent types compressed into midfield, meaning the race will fan wide off the bend as the bunch chases a single, unpressured leader. This controlled pace over a sprint trip on a flat, fair track is unlikely to generate a strong enough gallop to collapse the front-runner's advantage, instead producing a race where those closest to the pace as they turn for home hold the tactical edge. The race shape strongly favours horses that can race prominently or press from just off the pace, as hold-up horses will face a wall of traffic and a leader who has been gifted an easy lead — pure closers who need a fast pace to close into are at a structural disadvantage. Several runners are mapped out of their true role: Honour Your Dreams is the de facto front-runner by default rather than by nature, while Ten Cuidado, Sisters In The Sky, Daley T, and Rogue Rebellion are genuine hold-up types pushed into midfield who are unlikely to recapture their natural position in this race shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Honour Your Dreams Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Honour Your Dreams settles into an uncontested lead and the held-up field cannot close from the rear.
scenarios.body: She controls the tempo at a comfortable clip, arriving at the final furlong with reserves intact while the pursuing pack — strung across the track — burns energy closing the gap rather than lengthening past her; the Good going neither helps nor hinders, keeping conditions honest for a front-running display.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Pressurise
scenarios.trigger: If Geemann or Sisters In The Sky push forward aggressively early to sit on Honour Your Dreams's shoulder and force a contested pace.
scenarios.body: The front two burn through energy, and the horse best able to sustain a short burst off that pressure — likely one of the better-placed midfielders — emerges in the final 100 yards; Geemann's recent placed form in similar Good conditions makes him the most credible candidate to benefit from a slightly harder gallop.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Swoop Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is stronger than anticipated and the entire field fans wide in the straight, leaving daylight for genuine hold-up horses.
scenarios.body: With Honour Your Dreams potentially tiring if the pace quickens mid-race, a horse finishing with a sustained run from midfield could pick off tired rivals in the final furlong; Rogue Rebellion's consistent placed efforts at 6f on Good ground gives it the most plausible profile here, though the structural pace disadvantage keeps this outcome unlikely.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Handicap Compression
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so compressed that the field bunches turning in and the race becomes a sprint handicapper's lottery in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: With nine runners packed tightly and a muddling gallop, luck in running and draw become decisive rather than form or style; low-weight, unexposed runners could capitalise on a messy finish, though this scenario offers no structural advantage to any identifiable profile in this field.

watchPoints.text: Honour Your Dreams sets off alone on an uncontested lead — watch whether any rival pushes forward before the 4f pole to apply genuine pressure, as the absence of any challenger is the critical pace variable for this race.

Geemann ran only two days ago and any sign of flatness or reluctance in the preliminaries would dramatically reduce his chance, given his form otherwise represents the most credible threat to the front-runner.

Cici's Secret is flagged as fading in finishes and could drift right or crowd rivals in the closing stages — positioned in a compressed midfield on a flat track, any drift or late weakness from her could impede horses finishing on her outside.

Ten Cuidado and Daley T are both true hold-up types squeezed into a tactical midfield — watch their early positioning on the break, as either pushing forward or getting trapped wide could dramatically alter their chance in either direction.

Bath's 5½f track is flat and fair, offering no particular draw bias, but watch whether the field splits into two groups widening in the straight — horses drawn widest (high numbers) could find themselves covering extra ground if the pace stays low.

runners_data.name: Recon Mission
runners_data.note: A ten-year-old hold-up horse for Tony Carroll who has run six times on similar going without winning; Luke Morris takes over but recent form shows 3-3-5-6-6 and the horse's late-running style is poorly served by an uncontested-pace scenario here.
runners_data.comment: Recon Mission has been knocking at the door, third in each of his last two starts, and he returns here fit on just 11 days' rest with experience of today's trip and conditions; winless in his last five, he must convert promise into reward, but our rating of 61 marks him out as the one with the profile to do so.

runners_data.name: Call Time
runners_data.note: The only confirmed prominent racer in the field and well-positioned to inherit second if Wedgewood leads uncontested; Taylor Fisher rides for J S Moore and this five-year-old's five-furlong form at Bath-equivalent flat tracks makes this the most naturally suited tactical profile in the race.
runners_data.comment: Call Time has run over today's trip and going and steps back up in class with an encouraging third last time out, his form figures pointing to a live each-way threat; the main risk is that he remains winless in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Mart
runners_data.note: Last ran just a day ago which is a significant freshness concern; Ryan Kavanagh (3lb claim) partners this hold-up horse who has a placed effort at 5f on good, but the rapid turnaround and hold-up style are both negatives given the likely pace shape.
runners_data.comment: Rated highest in the field and carrying 132 lb from stall 8, Mart brings strong claims despite being winless in recent starts; second last time out shows he retains his form, though having run just one day ago, fitness is the question to answer.

runners_data.name: Stapleford Park
runners_data.note: A four-year-old hold-up type for Attwater with a second at Sandown among recent runs but no win from 15 runs on comparable going; Seamus Cronin's 5lb claim partially offsets the class concern, though the horse's rear-of-field tendencies leave it vulnerable in a moderately-paced 5f.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Stapleford Park at least has experience of today's trip and going and comes here fresh on an 11-day turnaround, though a second four starts back is the sole encouragement in a largely disappointing recent profile.

runners_data.name: Coolagh Magic
runners_data.note: A ten-year-old for Anthony Carson with genuine hold-up credentials — including a win on good at 6f — but bumped into the midfield on this map because the rear is oversubscribed; William Carson rides and the horse has real form to claim, though racing slightly forward of its comfort zone tempers the outlook.
runners_data.comment: Coolagh Magic won two starts back but has otherwise been out of the frame in recent starts, and our figures rank him eighth of ten in a field where his profile makes him hard to fancy, even if he has run over today's trip and going and returns fit on just 11 days' rest.

runners_data.name: Fancy Dancer
runners_data.note: A four-year-old for Hayley Burton whose recent placed efforts at 5f on standard ground are solid claims, and Saffie Osborne takes the ride; the horse is a true hold-up type shown in midfield because of overcrowding at the rear, meaning it will not naturally find the tactical position it needs.
runners_data.comment: Fancy Dancer has been runner-up twice in her last six starts, including second last time out just seven days ago, and has run over today's distance and going — a consistent threat even if she remains yet to win, with the main risk being that unplaced effort two starts back.

runners_data.name: Jackie Brown
runners_data.note: Six-year-old for Adrian Wintle with a win on firm, placed efforts on good and a useful recent 2nd/3rd run profile; Finley Marsh rides and the horse has meaningful course-type form, but its hold-up identity is squeezed by the crowded rear, leaving it reliant on a pace strong enough to bring it into contention.
runners_data.comment: Jackie Brown won two starts back but was only sixth last time out, and while she has run over today's trip and going before, the 129 lb burden is a stiff ask for a mare rated just 48 officially.

runners_data.name: Wedgewood
runners_data.note: The sole front-runner in the race and the pivot on which every scenario turns; Tom Marquand takes the reins for Tony Carroll after 72 days off, and while the freshness is a question mark, OR 47 at the bottom of the weights and the licence to lead uncontested on a flat 5f is a strong structural advantage.
runners_data.comment: Wedgewood showed her best when winning and recording back-to-back seconds in a productive mid-season spell, but two subsequent sixths suggest she has gone off the boil; having run over today's trip and going is a plus, though 72 days off the track adds a fitness query.

runners_data.name: Symbol Of Hope
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old for Grace Harris who has placed twice on firm and once on good in recent starts; Callum Hutchinson rides and the headgear (p) is noted, but the true hold-up profile placed in midfield by redistribution means this veteran needs more pace than Wedgewood alone is likely to generate.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Symbol Of Hope faces a stiff task here; the second-placed effort two runs back is a flicker of hope, and he has run over today's trip and going before, but the overall profile makes him hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: Hi Hoh Tonto
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old for Nick Littmoden returning after 114 days off — a significant layoff flag; Gina Mangan rides and the horse's best going figures are from good conditions, but the long absence combined with a genuine hold-up identity rerouted into a midfield slot makes this a speculative runner at best.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked ninth of ten on our figures, Hi Hoh Tonto faces a stiff task after 114 days off; he has run over today's trip and going before, and 126 lb from stall five are the modest positives to cling to.

races.paceDynamic: Wedgewood is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine pace rival to apply pressure, is set to stride into an uncontested lead from the gates and control tempo over this flat 5f Bath track. With good ground underfoot and a clear run to the front, Wedgewood can dictate a sustainable, metronomic gallop — not a suicidal blaze — which keeps the backmarkers honest but denies them a true test of finishing speed. The field behind is crowded with hold-up horses — Coolagh Magic, Fancy Dancer, Jackie Brown, Symbol Of Hope, and Hi Hoh Tonto — whose natural style is to come from off the pace, but the sheer volume of hold-up types means only the most forward-thinking among them will secure a genuinely prominent pitch; Call Time (P) is best placed to fill that space. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers and confirmed front-runners: a moderate, uncontested gallop set by Wedgewood will not generate the bunched finish or late sprint that pure closers need, and those who can sit handy without burning petrol early hold the decisive tactical edge.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Wedgewood Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Wedgewood breaks cleanly and settles into an uncontested lead, controlling tempo throughout.
scenarios.body: Wedgewood is able to set a comfortable, energy-conserving gallop over the flat 5f, producing a tactical test where the leader can quicken on their own terms in the final furlong. Horses who can sit prominently and respond to the injection of pace — such as Call Time — are best placed, while true hold-up horses are left with insufficient ground to make up.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Trade Blows
scenarios.trigger: If Call Time pushes up to challenge Wedgewood early, forcing a genuine pace duel through the first two furlongs.
scenarios.body: A contested lead heats up the early fractions, softening Wedgewood and Call Time and creating a stronger-than-expected early gallop that brings closers into play late.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to string the field out and hold-up horses find clear daylight in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: With the field spread across the track, the redistributed hold-up horses — Coolagh Magic, Jackie Brown, Fancy Dancer — could finish with a rattle if gaps materialise, though their mapped midfield positions are not their natural home and the scenario is conditional on the pace being far stronger than one front-runner typically generates.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Scrappy Muddled Affair
scenarios.trigger: If the field bunches and jostles for position early with no clean pace shape emerging due to crowding from the many hold-up types.
scenarios.body: A messy, compressed race with no clear sectional pattern can produce a random outcome where unexposed or in-form horses benefit from a fortunate position; Mart's recent form and Stapleford Park's prior placed effort are minor claims here.

watchPoints.text: Wedgewood (Tom Marquand) — 72 days off means a clean break and a fast start cannot be taken for granted; if Wedgewood misses the kick, the entire pace map collapses and the race becomes chaotic.

Call Time has headgear noted (p) and could push up aggressively to challenge Wedgewood; if Taylor Fisher elects to press the leader rather than sit just off, the steady-pace scenario shifts rapidly toward a pace duel that brings the hold-up horses into play.

Coolagh Magic and Jackie Brown — both genuine hold-up horses remapped to midfield — will be jostling for position in a congested middle pack; traffic problems in the final two furlongs are a live risk for both, which could frustrate their chances even if the pace suits.

Mart ran just one day ago and should be monitored in the preliminary and early stages for signs of fatigue or unwillingness; any underperformance from this horse is informative rather than surprising given the rapid turnaround.

Good ground confirmed throughout the card at Bath, consistent with the going report — no horse carries a going concern today, but the flat 5f configuration means there is no descent to aid hold-up horses and the premium on a clean early position is higher than at most courses.

races.name: Bath Country Race Day, Running 9 Till 5 Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Trooper
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up performer with 16f experience and Good-ground form, returning after 25 days; Neil Mulholland's runner has a modest sim-going record (0 wins) but the trip suits, and Luke Morris gives him tactical options from the rear — needs the pace to be strong enough to bring him into contention.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked ninth of ten on our figures, Trooper is hard to fancy at the weights carrying 135 lb, though he has run over today's trip before and 25 days off the track leaves him reasonably fresh.

runners_data.name: Basilette
runners_data.note: Has won and placed consistently over 14-18f on Good ground with a strong sim-going record (2W9P in 15 runs); as the race's lone confirmed front-runner she commands a significant positional advantage and George Downing can dictate every aspect of the tempo — the STYLE_FIT flag is noted but her natural prominence is entirely suited here.
runners_data.comment: Basilette caught the eye with a second last time out and a third three starts back, showing consistent ability at this level, and her experience over today's trip and going counts in her favour; the main risk is whether she can convert that placed form into a win off 133 lb.

runners_data.name: Just Adair
runners_data.note: Pat Cosgrave partners a four-year-old with five placings from ten similar-going runs, all at 12f — stepping up markedly to 1m6f here is the key question, as his form base is on shorter trips; tongue-strap applied, 36 days off, but trainer Jonjo & A.J. O'Neill have strong claims when fitting runners for a target.
runners_data.comment: Consistent enough to post three runner-up finishes in his last five starts, Just Adair has experience of today's going and our rating of 61 marks him as a genuine danger, though he remains winless in recent starts and will need to convert that placed form at last.

runners_data.name: Fram Castle
runners_data.note: A hold-up type with two recent placings at 14f and 16f on Good ground, giving her solid credentials for this trip; seven-pound claimer Alexandra Egan taking the mount is worth noting, visor headgear fitted, and her going record (0W4P) suggests consistency without the winning punch.
runners_data.comment: Fram Castle arrives here in decent nick, placing third last time out and second two starts back, giving him back-to-back placed efforts heading into this; he has run over today's trip and going before, and at 132 lb the weight is workable for a gelding rated 61 on our figures.

runners_data.name: Prophet Squeeze
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old whose natural style is to come from off the pace, though the density of hold-up types here means the rear will be crowded; Christian Howarth claims three pounds, but a zero-win record from 14 similar-going runs and recent form figures of 07R975 make it hard to construct a winning case.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, with a refused among those efforts, Prophet Squeeze faces a stiff ask carrying 129 lb and ranked eighth of ten on our figures; experience over today's going is the one small comfort in an otherwise hard-to-fancy profile.

runners_data.name: Cherry Cola
runners_data.note: A decade-old mare whose past headgear (p) and form figures of 365-86 over 13-17f show she handles this trip range; she is a true hold-up performer at heart, though 42 days off and a winless sim-going record (0W2P in 15 runs) temper expectations significantly.
runners_data.comment: Cherry Cola rates considerably higher than her official mark suggests, and having run over today's trip and going she arrives with genuine claims here; the concern is a winless recent run of five starts that underlines the need to convert.

runners_data.name: Alex The Great
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll's six-year-old wears a tongue-tie and has been placed at 12-14f on Good ground, but winless across 15 similar-going runs is a concern; his true style involves coming from off the pace and the congested hold-up group makes it hard for him to find a clear run, even if William Carson is an able navigator.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Alex The Great at least has experience of today's trip and going to call on, and back-to-back fourths suggest some consistency; however, an official rating of 45 and a 126 lb burden make life hard for him here.

runners_data.name: Nora Barnacle
runners_data.note: A four-year-old lightly raced in similar going (2 runs, 0W0P) and absent for 81 days — the layoff is the headline concern ahead of any tactical considerations; Ben Ffrench Davis claims five pounds, but six consecutive out-of-the-frame finishes and a step into this company make her an outsider in any scenario.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, with three sixths and a seventh among them, Nora Barnacle has been a model of disappointing consistency, and ranked bottom of the field on our figures she faces a stiff task, though she has run over today's trip and going and returns fresh after 81 days off.

runners_data.name: Notable Charm
runners_data.note: Marcus Tregoning's three-year-old is the least exposed on age and has the benefit of Rob Hornby, a high-quality jockey who will aim to get a clear passage; however, all five historic runs are at 8-12f, making this 1m6f trip a serious stamina test for a horse that has never been asked to stay this far.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Notable Charm does return quickly on 11 days' rest and has experience of today's going, but a pair of fourths among those efforts represents his best recently, and 122 lb is no help for a horse rated 50 officially.

runners_data.name: Lady Lauren
runners_data.note: Ed de Giles's three-year-old has placed twice from 13 similar-going runs but all form is at 8-12f, so like Notable Charm faces a genuine stamina question at this trip; no headgear, 27 days since last run, and Gina Mangan's claim of three pounds offers minor compensation for a horse yet to prove she stays.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Lady Lauren heads here 27 days after her latest fifth, and while she has run over today's going before and our rating edges above her official mark, a consistently modest recent profile makes it hard to fancy her strongly against a full field.

races.paceDynamic: Basilette is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 1m6f Bath handicap and should dictate from the front at a measured, uncontested gallop on Good ground, creating a genuinely sustainable pace rather than a searching test. With no rival likely to press her early, she controls tempo entirely — a significant positional advantage over a trip where Bath's undulations reward those who travel smoothly and avoid expending energy chasing. The majority of the field are true hold-up types (Trooper, Just Adair, Fram Castle, Notable Charm, Nora Barnacle, Alex The Great, Cherry Cola, Prophet Squeeze, Lady Lauren) who will settle in behind, meaning the race becomes a procession until the straight when closers attempt to reel in a front-runner who has conserved energy. This shape most favours the patient hold-up horse with a strong late finish over this extended trip, provided the pace is honest enough to bring them into contention — if Basilette dawdles, the race may be over before closers can fire. Several runners tagged as redistributed — including Notable Charm, Cherry Cola, Prophet Squeeze and Alex The Great — are genuine hold-up or prominent types who cannot all get their natural positions; of those, Basilette is the only one likely to actually secure the front, with Just Adair and Fram Castle the most plausible attendants.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Basilette Controls, Closers Chase
scenarios.trigger: If Basilette dictates a fair but uncontested pace and the hold-up horses produce their finishes from a compact midfield group.
scenarios.body: Basilette sets a rhythm that is honest enough to bring the closers into play turning in, but having saved energy throughout she proves difficult to reel in; hold-up horses with strong finishing form over this trip are best positioned to close but may just fall short.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Swamp Slow Gallop
scenarios.trigger: If Basilette crawls and the bunched field produces a sprint finish from the home straight.
scenarios.body: A slow early tempo compresses the field and removes any true test of stamina, turning the race into a flat-out dash over the final two furlongs; horses with a turn of foot from the back of a slowly-run race are at a premium.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Basilette Stays On Boldly
scenarios.trigger: If Basilette's controlled front-running proves too much to peg back and she extends clear in the straight.
scenarios.body: Running her own race from the front, Basilette gets first run on every rival and her recent course form over similar trips on Good ground makes her a genuine threat to hold on; hold-up horses struggle to make up enough ground on the Bath straight.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Stamina Test Sorts Field
scenarios.trigger: If a surprise challenger pushes Basilette along and a genuine strong gallop is set, turning this into a true stamina grind.
scenarios.body: A stronger pace than anticipated exposes those short of the full 1m6f trip and rewards the confirmed stayer who handles the extended distance in Good conditions; Trooper and Fram Castle, both with 16f+ form, would be most at home.

watchPoints.text: Basilette's early tempo is the single most important factor in this race — if George Downing elects to dawdle, the entire field bunches and her advantage as pace-setter evaporates; watch whether she is allowed to stride on or is restrained in the opening half-mile.

Just Adair is stepping up significantly in trip from a 12f base to 1m6f — Pat Cosgrave's ability to get him to relax and conserve energy in the early stages will be critical, and any sign of pulling hard could see him empty in the final quarter mile.

The Bath straight is relatively short for a 1m6f race and with most of this field holding up, traffic and positioning as the field rounds the final bend could be a significant factor — horses drawn or ridden wide may benefit from a cleaner passage.

Notable Charm and Lady Lauren are both three-year-olds being asked to stay 1m6f for the first time — their finishing efforts, even if modest, will provide useful stamina data, but punters should treat their chances with caution given the unproven trip.

Nora Barnacle returns after 81 days off and has never fired on All-Weather or Soft-leaning surfaces — watch her in the paddock for signs of fitness, as an underdone runner in a compact hold-up group could cause interference for those around her.

races.name: Regal Gaming Grand Gallop Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Sceptic
runners_data.note: Ryan Kavanagh (3lb claimer) rides this hold-up type for Ian Williams; won last time out over 8f on Standard (AW) and has some Good-ground form, but the style mismatch in a front-dominated race makes this a hard profile to win from — needs an unusually strong pace collapse.|
runners_data.comment: Sceptic has experience of today's distance and going, and a win four starts back gives his profile some substance, but a pair of fifth-place finishes in his last two runs and a ranking of tenth in a field of thirteen suggest he faces a stiff ask from stall 12 carrying 132 lb.

runners_data.name: Mbappe
runners_data.note: Won over 8f on Standard ground (AW) but has limited Similar-going form (2/15); a natural hold-up horse pushed into a midfield map position, with a STYLE_FIT of 0.91 cautioning against overrating his chances — headgear (p) noted.|
runners_data.comment: Showed a win five starts back and a third six starts back, but three subsequent efforts have brought nothing better than fifth, and his recent consistency is a concern; has run over today's trip and going, carries 131 lb from stall nine, and an 18-day break leaves fitness an open question.

runners_data.name: Electric Bass
runners_data.note: Drops sharply in trip from 10f-14f runs to a flat Bath mile, which may grant her enough stamina reserves to sustain the lead if she settles; Roger Teal has been busy with four winners from 12 (T14), and Dougie Costello is a strong booking for a front-runner at this level.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked near the foot of the field on our figures, Electric Bass faces a stiff task here; a third last time out and experience over today's trip and going offer faint encouragement, but 131 lb from stall four after a 48-day break makes this a tough ask.

runners_data.name: Thestral
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse by profile but with a placed effort on Good ground and a jockey booking in Jack Doughty; the 3yo age allowance is meaningful here, and a position tracking midfield rather than the very rear could work if the pace truly collapses — headgear noted (p).|
runners_data.comment: Thestral shaped with promise when third three starts back and second four starts back, and he returns here on a going and distance combination he has already encountered, with our rating of 65 suggesting he is ahead of his official mark; yet he remains winless in recent starts, which is the key concern.

runners_data.name: Galactic Glow
runners_data.note: See above — note entered under correct position in sequence.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts with a string of mid-pack and placed efforts, Galactic Glow is a difficult proposition ranked 11 of 13 on our figures, though he has run over today's trip and going before and steps back up fresh enough on 24 days' rest.

runners_data.name: Eagle Day
runners_data.note: Flagged as a horse that fades in finish, which is a significant concern in a pace-pressed race on this track; 31 days since last run and no wins or places on Similar going (6/15, 0W0P) — the finishing tendency makes this a difficult proposition regardless of scenario.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Eagle Day nevertheless shaped with promise when fourth at two of his last four outings and arrives here on a handy 10-lb pull between his official mark and our rating of 70, suggesting he retains untapped potential; he has run over today's trip and going, and 31 days between runs looks a sharp enough preparation.

runners_data.name: Wildfell
runners_data.note: Has been off the track 405 days — an enormous absence for a 6yo handicapper — and has zero wins or places in Similar going (4/15, 0W0P); fitness must be the dominant concern over any positional analysis, and the poor recent form string (79/00-) underlines that caution.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and off the track for 405 days, Wildfell faces a steep ask on fitness, yet his rating of 74 — highest among the 13 runners — and experience over today's trip and going mark him as a genuine threat if that layoff hasn't blunted his edge.

runners_data.name: Havana Club
runners_data.note: Won last time out over 8f on Good-ish ground and ran just 30 days ago — in form and on a going surface that suits; however, naturally a hold-up type accommodated in midfield due to field composition, meaning getting a clean run through 14 runners is the primary obstacle.|
runners_data.comment: Havana Club won two starts back and was third last time out, so there is recent form to like, but a sixth and a fourth deeper in his record temper enthusiasm; he has run over today's trip and going, carries 132 lb from stall five, and returns on a fair 30-day break.

runners_data.name: Blue Hero
runners_data.note: Has won twice in recent form including over 8f on Firm, and is trained by Adrian Wintle alongside Havana Club — potential stable interference in race plans; a genuine hold-up horse mapped to midfield because the field is saturated with similar types, and at age 8 needs things to fall right.|
runners_data.comment: Blue Hero arrives on the back of two wins in his last five starts, including a victory last time out, and has experience of today's distance and going; however, 33 days off the track introduces a fitness query and 132 lb from stall 13 is no small ask.

runners_data.name: Buckland Belle
runners_data.note: Prominent-style runner for Tom Marquand and Ollie Sangster with the most consistent Good-ground record in this field (6/14 sim-going, 2W6P); ran just nine days ago, which may leave a fitness question, but her pattern of tracking the pace and finishing with a clean run suits this shape ideally.|
runners_data.comment: Consistent but not dominant, Buckland Belle has placed in five of her last six starts with a win three starts back, yet a speed rating of 56 leaves a question mark against her; she has run over today's trip and returns quickly on nine days' rest from stall one carrying 130 lb.

runners_data.name: Lovely Jubly
runners_data.note: Listed as Non Runner — no further analysis applicable; had the double flag of fading in finish and a STYLE_FIT discount as a redistributed hold-up type.|
runners_data.comment: Lovely Jubly won last time out but that was 56 days ago, she ranks last on our figures in a 13-runner field, and carrying 130 lb from stall 14 adds to the concerns, though she has run over today's trip and that recent win is a genuine positive.

runners_data.name: Amathus
runners_data.note: Best similar-going record in the field among the redistribted group (12/15, 3W4P) and wore a visor last time; at age 9 the profile is declining, but this veteran clearly handles Good ground well — the challenge is getting a clear run through 14 horses from a hold-up position.|
runners_data.comment: Amathus won two starts back but has since finished fifth, and his wider form is patchy; he has run over today's trip and going, carries 129 lb from stall two, and at a rating of 62 holds claims without being the most compelling option in this field.

runners_data.name: Malakai Kite
runners_data.note: Unclassified style (U) makes this 3yo hard to place in the race map; has been placed consistently on Good ground (3/4 sim-going, 0W2P) and wears a hood — Luke Morris is an astute jockey who could exploit positional flexibility if the race unfolds chaotically.|
runners_data.comment: Malakai Kite has been knocking on the door, third last time out and third again three starts back, showing consistent intent over today's trip and going; winless in recent starts is the concern, but our rating of 64 suggests he is capable of going one better.

runners_data.name: Who Is Alice
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for Grace Harris, who is in excellent recent form (6/25 over 14 days); drops back to a mile having raced mainly at shorter, but connections are likely to press forward regardless — the contested early duel with Electric Bass is the key tactical question for her stamina.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked last on our figures, Who Is Alice makes for a difficult each-way proposition; she does return quickly on nine days' rest, has experience over today's trip and going, and draws stall three carrying 127 lb.

races.paceDynamic: Who Is Alice and Electric Bass are the two confirmed front-runners, and with both likely to push forward from the outset, this race will be run at an honest, contested gallop from the first furlong — neither will concede the lead without a fight, setting up a genuine pace duel through the early stages of this flat Bath mile. That sustained early pressure will stretch the field and make it difficult for closers to get a true tactical breather, meaning the race tempo should be consistent rather than end-loaded. Buckland Belle is the most natural prominent-style runner capable of tracking in second or third without overextending, and she is best placed to capitalise if the two leaders press each other into submission. The field holds more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate at the rear — Mbappe, Blue Hero, Havana Club, Galactic Glow, and Amathus are all genuine hold-up horses redistributed into midfield, and in a 14-runner field with a strong pace bias, only those mapping closest to the front — particularly Buckland Belle and any horse capable of tracking within three lengths of the leaders — are positioned to pounce when the pace collapses in the final two furlongs. This race shape clearly favours prominent-stalking types with tactical speed, as the contested lead will set up those travelling just behind rather than those forced wide or deep in the field.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Stalker Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Who Is Alice and Electric Bass press each other hard enough to exhaust both by the two-furlong pole, leaving the prominent stalker to collar them.
scenarios.body: The two leaders burn energy fighting for early supremacy, setting a tempo that suits a horse travelling smoothly just behind; once the pace collapses entering the final quarter-mile, the stalker has a clear run to the line. This shape strongly benefits Buckland Belle, who has the course form, consistent Good-ground record and the tactical position to pounce precisely when the front pair weaken.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Leaders Last Long
scenarios.trigger: If Electric Bass or Who Is Alice settles slightly and is not fully pressed, managing enough to sustain their gallop into the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A more economical front-runner who finds a rhythm rather than being fully tested can exploit a field of redistributed hold-up horses who cannot easily close from deep; the prominent pace-setter who dictates alone clear of trouble holds a significant advantage on a flat course that rewards sustained galloping. Electric Bass, dropping back in trip from recent 10f-plus runs, may have the stamina reserves to see it out if she controls things, while Who Is Alice's handler is in fine recent form with six winners from 25 runners over 14 days.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Surge Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is truly fierce and collapses sharply, allowing the deepest-lying runners to make up unexpected ground in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A genuine meltdown of the front two could, in theory, allow horses sitting midfield to finish strongly, but most of the horses occupying that zone are redistributed hold-up types who are racing out of role with STYLE_FIT discounts — making a clean finishing run hard to deliver in a 14-runner field. Galactic Glow has the strongest Good-going record of the midfield group and Amathus has shown winning form on similar ground, giving them the best residual claims if this shape materialises against the odds.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos, Race Falls Apart
scenarios.trigger: If the pace duel causes significant bunching or interference through the field, scrambling normal positional hierarchies and producing a messy, tactical sprint finish.
scenarios.body: In a 14-runner field with this many horses unable to find their natural position, racing incidents, wide draws, and crowding are elevated risks; a horse that avoids trouble and has a clean passage could benefit regardless of style. Malakai Kite, whose style is unclassified and who has been consistently placed on Good ground, could exploit a disorderly finish, while Havana Club's course experience and recent win give it residual claims.

watchPoints.text: Who Is Alice and Electric Bass will both be angling for the front from the gates — watch the first furlong closely, as any bumping or jostling between these two pace-setters could unsettle either and escalate the contest into a genuine burn-up that destroys both of their winning chances.

Wildfell returns from a 405-day absence and has shown no signs of form in recent outings — watch for early signs of struggle that could cause interference in a 14-runner field if the horse fails to maintain pace.

Eagle Day is flagged as a horse that fades in the finish; in a race with a strong early pace, a fading runner in the pack entering the final furlong is a significant interference risk for closers trying to make their run.

Lovely Jubly is a Non Runner — confirm at the off that the field is 13 runners, as the absence removes one hold-up type and may fractionally ease the positional congestion at the rear, giving the remaining redistributed horses marginally more room.

Buckland Belle ran just nine days ago — watch her in the pre-race paddock and early strides for any sign of dullness or stiffness, as a horse second time out in quick succession can occasionally show below-par early pace even when well enough to compete.

races.name: British EBF Fillies' Handicap Stakes (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Quebella
runners_data.note: Owen Burrows filly who has shown a patient hold-up style across her five runs, earning a place in this race's most favoured tactical position; 82 days off the track is the one mild concern, but her three placings on similar going (3/8 record) and proven stamina at 12f suggest the freshness is manageable for Jamie Spencer, a master at sitting cold in small fields.
runners_data.comment: Quebella has shown consistent form with three thirds in her last five starts, and has run over today's distance and going before; winless in recent starts, but her rating of 97 makes her the one to beat from stall 5, with 142 lb to carry after 82 days off the most notable query.

runners_data.name: Pierian
runners_data.note: William Haggas's three-year-old has the class edge (OR 87) and a sparkling 2W3P record across five runs on Good, and Tom Marquand will likely press immediately for the lead — the problem is Spirit Of Jura and Asset will not yield cheaply, so her chance depends entirely on whether she can dominate and conserve enough for Bath's punishing finish.
runners_data.comment: Pierian won twice in her last five starts and has experience of today's trip and conditions, making her a strong player from stall one carrying 138 lb; the concern is she was unplaced last time out.

runners_data.name: Spirit Of Jura
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's mare is a proven front-runner who has contested the lead in the majority of her 15 starts on Good, and while she has shown grit (1W4P) she has also been beaten at 13f and 14f before; at OR 79 she is outrated, and her role here may be to be a pace-maker for the better horses whether she intends it or not.
runners_data.comment: Placed third last time out and second three starts back, Spirit Of Jura has shown consistent ability to mix it at this level, and her rating of 88 makes her a clear threat to the top-ranked runner; the risk is she has been winless in her last six starts.

runners_data.name: Mythical Bird
runners_data.note: Hughie Morrison's four-year-old carries a prominent style and arrives on a sharp 21-day turnaround after winning a 1m handicap on Good at OR 77; stepping up significantly in trip to 1m3½f is a genuine stamina question given her best recent form has come at 1m and 1m2f, and Rob Hornby will need to find a sensible position behind the speed battle.
runners_data.comment: Mythical Bird won last time out and was third two starts back, giving her a lively profile in recent starts, and she has experience of today's going; the main risk is whether she can reproduce that form under a hefty 136 lb.

runners_data.name: Aravalli
runners_data.note: Joe Tickle's three-year-old arrives in explosive form — four wins from five on Good, including back-to-back 1m2f victories — and Taylor Fisher will aim to track the pace from a prominent position without getting embroiled in the front-running war; the step to 1m3½f is an unknown but her work ethic on Good ground suggests she will stay, and her OR 82 represents solid recent improvement.
runners_data.comment: Aravalli arrives in good heart with back-to-back wins and four victories in her last six starts, and she has run over today's trip before, but our figures rank her last of six in this field and make her hard to fancy at the weights.

runners_data.name: Asset
runners_data.note: Sir Mark Prescott's filly has a natural front-running profile and a busy yard (T14: 6/14) with intent; she has yet to win beyond 1m on Good (best effort a win at 1m on Good), so the trip and the presence of two other confirmed leaders pressing her from the start makes this a high-attrition assignment, and Luke Morris may struggle to find daylight if she fades.
runners_data.comment: Ranked fifth of six on our figures, Asset faces a stiff task at the weights carrying 129 lb, and a speed rating of 72 leaves her looking well held on paper; she does bring recent consistency, third last time out and a winner two starts back, plus going experience in her favour.

races.paceDynamic: Pierian, Spirit Of Jura, and Asset all carry confirmed front-running profiles over 1m3½f at Bath, meaning this race will be lit up from the gates with three fillies contesting the early lead and ensuring a genuinely strong, honest gallop throughout. Pierian (Haggas/Marquand) is the classiest of the trio and most likely to secure the prime position on the rail, but Spirit Of Jura and Asset will push and harry her every step, creating a contested pace that will drain stamina reserves long before the home turn. Bath's uphill finish further amplifies the punishing effect of a hot early tempo over this trip, meaning those who race prominently and burn their fuel fighting for position are unlikely to find much extra when the race ignites. This shape strongly favours closers or patient hold-up horses with proven stamina — Quebella and Aravalli, both capable of switching off and hitting the line late, sit in the most tactically advantageous position in a race where the pace is doing their work.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Closers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the three-way battle for the lead produces a genuinely fast early gallop that shreds the front runners' stamina by the home turn.
scenarios.body: Pierian, Spirit Of Jura, and Asset burn each other off through the first mile, setting up a truly run race that plays right into the hands of hold-up and prominent fillies arriving fresh and strong.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Haggas Filly Controls, Stays On
scenarios.trigger: If Pierian asserts quickly, the others yield, and she dictates a measured pace from the front.
scenarios.body: A controlled lead at Haggas's hands removes the chaos, Pierian conserves energy and her superior class sees her stay on powerfully up the Bath hill, resisting all challengers.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Quickens Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is honest but not brutal and a prominent-running filly times her run to perfection rounding the final bend.
scenarios.body: Aravalli, in superb recent form with four wins from her last five including consecutive 1m2f victories on Good, moves smoothly into contention and her relentless finish proves too good for tired front runners.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Muddle, No Benefit
scenarios.trigger: If contradictory tactics produce a slow opening that bunches the field and the race turns on a sprint up the hill.
scenarios.body: Front runners fail to dominate early, the race becomes a falsely run affair, and a filly with a turn of foot on Good ground seizes the moment — but this scenario is improbable given the volume of genuine speed in the field.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Pierian, Spirit Of Jura, and Asset establish a pecking order immediately — if all three are locked in a genuine three-way battle through the first half-mile, the race is almost certainly being set up for Quebella or Aravalli arriving late.

Aravalli's step up to 1m3½f is unproven; if she over-races in the prominent group tracking three contested leaders, Taylor Fisher will need to be ice-cool to preserve her stamina for the climb to the finish.

Mythical Bird's trip rise from 1m to 1m3½f is the starkest distance jump in the field — Rob Hornby must secure a position far enough off the speed to avoid being swept up in the carnage, but close enough to strike if the front runners implode.

Bath's uphill straight disproportionately punishes fillies who have spent energy early; any runner who has been competitive through the first five furlongs of this race is likely to find little extra in the final 2½f, making the closing sectionals critical to track.

Going is confirmed Good throughout the card with no deterioration reported — no going concerns for any runner, so ground will not be a differentiating factor and the race will be decided purely on stamina, tactics, and class.

runners_data.name: Shaffron
runners_data.note: Returns from 111 days off for David Menuisier, who wins at a modest 14-day strike rate; has placed over 12f on good ground once from seven attempts at similar going, so the surface is fine but the long layoff is the key question mark, and a hold-up style means she needs a proper tempo to get involved.
runners_data.comment: Shaffron returns from 111 days off carrying 135 lb from stall four, and has run over today's trip and going before — her third last time out shows she can threaten, though she remains winless in recent starts and the layoff is the chief concern.

runners_data.name: Jodhpur Blue
runners_data.note: Ian Williams runner carrying a hood, 30 days since last run and 30 days looks fresh enough; has placed six times in fifteen similar-going starts without winning, suggesting a horse that runs consistently without always delivering — a hold-up type who needs the race to truly flow.
runners_data.comment: Jodhpur Blue has shown consistent placing ability, finishing third last time out and second three starts back, and he has run over today's trip and going before. Carrying 135 lb from stall three, our rating of 69 marks him as the one to beat, though he remains winless in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Trojan Truth
runners_data.note: Strong recent form in similar conditions (10 runs, 3 wins, 6 places on good) makes this the stand-out for surface suitability; wears a hood and runs for a small Ed de Giles yard, and while his natural style is to come from well off the pace, in this small field he is unlikely to find the rearmost position he truly wants, potentially blunting his late charge.
runners_data.comment: Trojan Truth showed plenty of grit with a second two starts back and a third three starts back, and he has experience over today's trip and going to call on; drawn in stall one carrying 134 lb, the main concern is that he remains winless in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Offiah's Boy
runners_data.note: Won over 9f on good ground and placed at 10f on the same surface — the step up to 1m3½f is the main unknown; a natural hold-up horse who has found his groove in this going, though operating out of his preferred deep position in a six-runner field will make life harder than his recent form figure of 1-2-3 implies.
runners_data.comment: Ranked fifth of six on our figures and rated below his official mark, Offiah's Boy makes the case hard to build, though he does bring experience of today's trip and going, a win two starts back, and a third last time out suggesting some residual form.

runners_data.name: Belle Amie
runners_data.note: The race's sole confirmed front-runner for David Simcock, who has hit two winners in eleven attempts over 14 days — healthy stable form; has won twice and placed twice in 13 similar-going starts, and controlling a small field from the front with no genuine challenger suits her well, though the STYLE_FIT flag flags she is not a dominant pace machine.
runners_data.comment: Belle Amie arrives on the back of a third last time out and a win three starts back, with experience over today's trip and going working in her favour at a manageable 130 lb from stall five. The risk is her rating edge over the field is slim.

runners_data.name: Douglas Dc
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll's veteran, eight years old and 15 days fresh, with four wins from 43 in a purple patch for the yard over 14 days (4/43 strike rate); handles good and has placed four times in 12 similar-going runs, but his prominent style means he is more likely to press Belle Amie than lead — a key tactical figure in determining how hard the front end is contested.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and ranked last on our figures, Douglas Dc faces a stiff task here, though second two starts back suggests some capability, he has run over today's trip and going before, and 15 days since his last outing leaves him reasonably fresh.

races.paceDynamic: Belle Amie is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with only Douglas Dc likely to push forward alongside her, she faces no genuine pressure for the lead on this flat Bath circuit over 1m3½f on good ground. That means a controlled, measured gallop from the front, with Belle Amie able to dictate tempo and conserve energy through the long middle portion of the race before the final bend. Trojan Truth and Offiah's Boy are genuine hold-up horses but, with the field already carrying more closers than the map can accommodate at the rear, they are likely to be shuffled into mid-division rather than finding their true position deep in the pack, blunting the late kick they rely upon. This race shape strongly favours the prominent or front-running profile — a sustainable gallop set by Belle Amie with minimal disruption creates ideal conditions for those who can travel close to the pace and pounce in the straight, rather than those needing a truly honest tempo to generate a closing run.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Belle Amie Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Belle Amie secures the lead unchallenged and Douglas Dc settles just behind without applying pressure, creating a sedate, well-regulated tempo.
scenarios.body: Belle Amie sets a comfortable pace, conserving enough to quicken into the straight, while Douglas Dc or any prominent-tracking rival benefits from cover just off the pace; the hold-up horses are denied the strong gallop needed to close from off the bridle.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Land Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is stronger than expected and genuine closers find enough room and momentum to finish through beaten rivals in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Trojan Truth, with the best recent record in similar good-ground form (3W6P in matching conditions), would be the primary beneficiary if a genuine gallop develops; Offiah's Boy, who clearly handles good ground, would also be in the mix if traffic clears in time.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Belle Amie and Douglas Dc set an unrealistically slow early pace that causes the race to turn into a sprint finish, catching the leaders flat-footed.
scenarios.body: A dawdle suits horses with tactical speed who have been travelling comfortably in mid-division; Jodhpur Blue, who has placed six times in fifteen similar-going starts and handles this trip, could benefit from a sharp late injection of pace.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos at Front, Field Bunches
scenarios.trigger: If Douglas Dc applies unexpected pressure early or the field concertinas, disrupting Belle Amie's rhythm and producing a ragged, unpredictable race.
scenarios.body: A messy pace scenario opens the race up and makes the result harder to call on running style alone; Shaffron, fresh off a 111-day break with form over this trip and a capable trainer in Menuisier, is the speculative beneficiary if a rough pace suits a horse running fresh.

watchPoints.text: Belle Amie's ability to control the tempo unchallenged is the single biggest race-shaping factor — if Douglas Dc applies pressure before the home turn, the whole pace dynamic collapses.

Trojan Truth's redistribution from hold-up to mid-division is significant — watch how Luke Morris positions him in the first furlong, as racing against his instincts could see him use energy too early.
Offiah's Boy faces a career-longest trip here at 1m3½f; if he finds the extra distance beyond his stamina, his usual late flourish may not materialise in the closing stages.

With only six runners on a flat track and good ground, draw and early positioning could matter more than usual — watch which horses are slow into stride at the off, as gaps form quickly in small fields.

Bath's final climb into the straight rewards horses travelling well within themselves at the two-furlong pole — any prominent or pace-prominent runner still on the bridle at that point should be noted.
